newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil - Prices stable, but supplies ample.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil - Prices stable, but supplies ample.

text.p: High sulphur fuel oil prices on Wednesday ended steady after firm swaps quotes offset bearish sentiment in the current weak cash market amid fresh buying interest, traders said.
February swaps were last quoted at $99.00/$99.50 per tonne, up from Tuesday's $98.00/$99.50 and tracking the gains in crude.

In the Singapore cash market, two bids were seen at $97.00 a tonne for February loading supplies against an offer from a Singapore-based trader for a 20,000-tonne cargo of 180 centistoke supplies at $99.50 a tonne for February 17-21 loading.
But healthy supplies still undermined the cash market, traders said.
"February looks bad but fundamentals should recover in March after the Chinese return to buy after the holidays," said a trader.
Traders said South Korean supplies remained on offer. They said bids were at a 50-cent discount against offers at par to a dollar per tonne premium to Singapore spot quotes for February loading.

They said Japanese supplies were also heard offered at a dollar premium to Singapore spot quotes on a FOB Japan basis. Three Kuwaiti cargoes were heard sold at between 75 cents and a dollar premium to Singapore spot quotes on a c+f Singapore basis for delivery in February. One cargo was heard still seeking a buyer as Kuwait exported four cargoes in February, traders said.
While some traders said two to three Mideast cargoes heading towards Singapore remained unplaced, others said these cargoes had been committed earlier.
India issued a tender to buy 60,000 tonnes of fuel oil for delivery in February. Traders said Indian demand would help take out some length in the market.
LSWR prices eased as the market sentiment remained bearish with traders citing poor demand and ample supplies amid a closed arbitrage window to the west.
(Prices in dollars per tonne, unless stated)
